The problem

Service providers are running blind.

Not a guess — it is what the market looks like across Egypt and the Gulf.

They run on WhatsApp and spreadsheets

Bookings in chat threads, prices in a notebook, no record of what a customer asked for last time.

They have no online discoverability

A salon or a photographer with no page, no listing and no search presence exists only to people who already know them.

They cannot distribute across channels

No way to be in a marketplace, on social, and in a booking flow at once — so they pick one and lose the rest.

The product

A platform, not a directory.

Three layers, each one useful alone and worth more together.

Marketplace

Customers find, compare and book services. Providers get demand they did not have to chase.

Provider storefront

Each provider gets a real online presence, a booking flow and a catalogue — set up in minutes, not a web project.

Growth Engine

A full marketing operation embedded in the platform: research, offer design, creative, paid traffic, lead qualification and an optimisation loop.

How it works

The Growth Engine is the moat.

Every marketplace can list providers. This runs their marketing for them, and step one is free — which is how a provider becomes a subscriber.

  1. 01

    Market research

    Real demand in the provider's city: what sells, at what price, against whom. Free, and included in the base plan — the hook.

  2. 02

    One hero offer

    A single focused service instead of a menu. Complexity removed, decisions made faster.

  3. 03

    Conversion asset

    A WhatsApp-ready booking page with a clear price, the benefit and one call to action.

  4. 04

    Traffic injection

    Local Facebook and Instagram campaigns, radius and interest targeted, on a controlled budget.

  5. 05

    Lead qualification

    WhatsApp question flows filter for budget, date and location, so only serious leads reach the provider.

  6. 06

    Closing and follow-up

    Arabic reply scripts, objection handling for the real ones — «غالي», «هفكر» — and automated sequences.

  7. 07

    Optimisation loop

    Weekly: scale what worked, kill what did not, drive cost per lead down. This is the part that compounds.

The model

Subscription first, wallet second.

The engine is not sold separately. It is quota inside a plan, and overflow draws on a wallet the provider already funds.

Three plans

Starter is influencer campaigns only. Pro adds a lead pipeline. Premium unlocks paid ads, AI creative and squad management.

Quota, then wallet

Exceed the plan and the system reserves against the provider wallet, executes, then settles — so usage above plan is revenue, not friction.

Hybrid commission

Influencers earn a base milestone per deliverable plus performance commission, multiplied by tier and reputation.

Real settlement

Attribution to commission ledger to wallet to payout, via InstaPay, Vodafone Cash or bank.

The ask

What the money is for.

Not engineering. The engineering is done and paid for.

  • Provider acquisitionThe first hundred paying providers in one city, so the funnel is measured rather than modelled.
  • Ad float for the engineThe Growth Engine spends on behalf of providers before they scale. That float is working capital, not cost.
  • A second operatorToday one person carries the product, the platform and the roadmap. That is the constraint, and it is not a technical one.
  • The iOS launchThe app is signed and ready. Publishing it is days of work — what it needs is the decision and the store presence to point at.
